title: HBM DRAM stack cost and supply scaling
bottleneck: High-bandwidth memory stacks DRAM dies vertically with TSVs to feed AI accelerators, but HBM is far more expensive per bit than conventional DRAM, requires custom base-die logic, and its supply chain is concentrated among three vendors. Stacking more layers (12-high, 16-high) increases thermal stress and test complexity, and HBM consumes package area and power budget that could otherwise go to compute.
why_it_blocks: AI training throughput is increasingly memory-bandwidth-bound; HBM cost and availability directly set the price and supply of every flagship AI chip. A supply crunch or cost plateau in HBM propagates into slower AI scaling and higher inference prices.
current_state: HBM3E is shipping in volume for current AI accelerators, with HBM4 on roadmaps adding wider interfaces. Vendors are expanding capacity, but pricing remains elevated and next-gen stacks face thermal and yield learning curves.
